title: Finite normalization over a dense open of an excellent scheme
statement:
Let $X$ be a reduced Noetherian excellent scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-exc-excellent-ring], where Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and excellent means that every affine open has excellent coordinate ring, and let $
u:X^
u	o X$ be its componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. Then $
u$ is finite and surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $X^
u$ is Noetherian excellent, and every local ring of $X^
u$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. There is a dense open subscheme $U\subseteq X$ containing every generic point of $X$ [def-sc-generic-point] such that $
u^{-1}U	o U$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-open-immersion]. The empty scheme is allowed, with $U$ empty.

source.place: Tags 035S (lemma-nagata-normalization), 035Q (lemma-normalization-normal), and 0BAJ (lemma-birational-isomorphism-over-dense-open); excellence via More on Algebra Tags 07QV and 07QU

proof.text: If $X=\varnothing$, its componentwise normalization is the empty coproduct, its map is finite and surjective, all local-ring conditions are vacuous, and $U=\varnothing$ works. Henceforth allow nonempty affine opens. On every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, the affine-chart lemma identifies $\nu^{-1}(V)$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_i B_i)$, where $B_i$ is the integral closure of $A/\mathfrak p_i$ in $K_i=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p_i)$ and the $\mathfrak p_i$ are the finitely many minimal primes. In particular $\nu$ is affine, and the same chart is the disjoint union of the open subschemes $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$.

source.place: lemma-description-normalization (035P), affine description; empty componentwise construction

proof.text: The ring $A$ is excellent by hypothesis, hence quasi-excellent by definition and Nagata by the cited excellence theorem. Thus, by the definition of a Nagata ring, every $A/\mathfrak p_i$ is N-2. Apply its N-2 property to the degree-one extension $K_i/K_i$: each $B_i$ is a finite $A/\mathfrak p_i$-module. Its module generators also generate it over $A$, since the $A$-action factors through the surjection $A\to A/\mathfrak p_i$. The finitely many tuples supported in one coordinate and containing these generators generate $\prod_i B_i$ over $A$. Consequently every affine chart from Step 1 has a finite structural ring map, so $\nu$ is finite by the definition of a finite morphism.

source.place: lemma-nagata-normalization (035S), direct affine proof; more-algebra.tex lemma-quasi-excellent-nagata (07QV)

proof.text: For each $i$, the inclusion $A/\mathfrak p_i\hookrightarrow B_i\subseteq K_i$ is injective and integral, since $B_i$ consists of the elements integral over $A/\mathfrak p_i$. Lying over gives a prime of $B_i$ above every prime of $A/\mathfrak p_i$. Thus the image of $\operatorname{Spec}B_i\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is $V(\mathfrak p_i)$. These are the irreducible components of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and cover it. The affine description in Step 1 therefore makes $\nu$ surjective on every affine open and hence on $X$.

source.place: lemma-normalization-normal (035Q)(2), surjectivity; algebra.tex lying over for integral injections

proof.text: Apply the integral-closure normal-domain lemma to $A/\mathfrak p_i$ and the degree-one extension $K_i/K_i$. It gives that $B_i$ is a normal domain. Every point of $X^\nu$ lies in one of the affine open summands $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ of Step 1. Its local ring is $(B_i)_{\mathfrak q}$ by the affine stalk theorem, and this is a normal domain by localization of normal domains (the prime complement does not contain zero). Thus every local ring of $X^\nu$ is an integrally closed domain.

By Step 2 each $B_i$ is finite as an $A$-module. A finite set of module generators also generates $B_i$ as an $A$-algebra, so finite-type stability of excellence gives that $B_i$ is excellent. The spectra of these rings, over all affine opens of $X$, form an affine open cover of $X^
u$. The excellence affine-cover theorem therefore gives excellence on every affine open of $X^
u$. To check global Noetherianness, choose a finite affine cover of $X$, using its quasi-compactness. Each inverse image has only finitely many of the affine summands in Step 1, and their excellent coordinate rings are Noetherian by definition. Together these give a finite affine cover of $X^
u$ by spectra of Noetherian rings. It is locally Noetherian by definition; it is quasi-compact because each affine is quasi-compact by the cited affine-scheme theorem and there are finitely many of them. This is precisely the Noetherian-scheme convention in the statement.

Enumerate the finitely many irreducible components $Z_1,\ldots,Z_r$ of $X$, with their unique generic points $\eta_i$ supplied by scheme sobriety. For each $i$, the open $X\setminus\bigcup_{j\ne i}Z_j$ contains $\eta_i$ and meets no other component. The affine-open basis theorem supplies an affine open neighbourhood $W_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ of $\eta_i$ inside it. Its topological space is an open subspace of the irreducible space $Z_i$, so is irreducible; it is reduced as an open of $X$. Hence $R_i$ is a domain. These $W_i$ need not cover $X$; only the generic points must lie in them.

source.place: lemma-birational-isomorphism-over-dense-open (0BAJ), reduction to an irreducible affine open for each component

proof.text:
On $W_i$, Step 1 has one summand: $
u^{-1}(W_i)=\operatorname{Spec}C_i$, where $R_i\subseteq C_i\subseteq\operatorname{Frac}(R_i)$ is the integral closure, finite over $R_i$ by Step 2. Choose module generators $c_1,\ldots,c_m$, and write $c_j=a_j/b_j$ with $0
e b_j\in R_i$. Let $s_i=\prod_j b_j$, taking $s_i=1$ if the list is empty. Then $s_i
e0$ and every generator lies in $(R_i)_{s_i}$, so $(C_i)_{s_i}\subseteq(R_i)_{s_i}$; the reverse inclusion follows from $R_i\subseteq C_i$, giving equality inside the fraction field. Integral closure commutes with localization, so the affine-chart lemma on $D(s_i)\subseteq W_i$ identifies its inverse image with $\operatorname{Spec}(C_i)_{s_i}$ and its restriction map with this equality. It is an isomorphism. The open $D(s_i)$ contains $\eta_i$ because $s_i
e0$.

source.place: lemma-birational-isomorphism-over-dense-open (0BAJ), finite birational affine case written out using module generators; algebra.tex lemma-integral-closure-localize (0307)

proof.text:
Put $U= igcup_{i=1}^r D(s_i)$, each principal open being viewed as an open of $X$ through $W_i$. The restriction of $
u$ over each $D(s_i)$ is an isomorphism by Step 7. Their inverse morphisms agree on overlaps: each is an inverse of the same restricted morphism, and a two-sided inverse is unique. Their continuous maps define a continuous map $U	o
u^{-1}(U)$ because the domains are an open cover. Their maps on structure sheaves agree on overlaps and glue by the sheaf axiom; on stalks the resulting homomorphisms are the local inverse isomorphisms and hence local. This defines a scheme morphism, whose two composites are identities on the covering opens and thus globally. It is an inverse of $
u^{-1}(U)	o U$. Every $\eta_i$ belongs to $U$, so its closure contains every $Z_i=\overline{\{\eta_i\}}$ and is all of $X$. Thus $U$ is dense and has the required generic-point and isomorphism properties.

source.place: lemma-birational-isomorphism-over-dense-open (0BAJ), assembly of the componentwise dense opens

split_report.summary: Proved the normalization preparation from its affine integral-closure product description. Excellence gives Nagata rings and hence finite closure modules; lying over gives surjectivity, localization gives normal stalks, and finite-type stability gives excellence and Noetherianness. A finite set of module-generator denominators constructs an isomorphism open around every generic point. Added one statement-only affine-chart interface, without moving any conclusion clause into it. Clarified only the existing Noetherian/excellent scheme conventions; the mathematical statement is unchanged.
split_report.blueprint: The normalization preparation requested by descendant lem-per-potential-dualizing-uniqueness Step 3 in the dimension-normalized duality branch from lem-per-artin-gabber-affine-curve; realizes the existing blueprint.from place and ancestry, without changing the perverse unit or its route.

tool_uses.why: The generic commutative-algebra theorem supplies Nagata finiteness for excellent affine rings; no node of this perverse-sheaf unit gives it.
Generic stability of excellence is needed for the finite affine normalization algebras; it does not replace a step of the perverse-sheaf unit.
Generic locality of excellence turns the normalization affine cover into the all-affine excellence convention; no local theorem of this unit supplies it.
Basic quasi-compactness of affine schemes is needed to turn the finite normalization chart cover into quasi-compactness of the normalization.
Generic points of the finitely many irreducible components are needed in the dense-open construction.
Affine neighbourhoods inside the open avoiding the other components are needed; no perverse-sheaf argument supplies this scheme topology fact.

The item gives its parent (lem-per-potential-dualizing-uniqueness Step 3) exactly what that step uses: a finite surjective map with normal source, an isomorphism over a dense open containing every generic point, and Noetherian excellence preserved. The Noetherian and excellent conventions it spells out are the standard ones and don't make the item easier. Steps: Step 2 gets finiteness from excellent ⇒ quasi-excellent ⇒ Nagata, then N-2 with L=K_i, product over the components and the finite-morphism definition. Step 3 gets surjectivity from lying over, with the V(p_i) covering Spec A. Step 4 gets normality from the integral closure being a normal domain, the affine stalk lemma and localization. Step 5 gets excellence from 07QU with S={1} and the 0HAB affine-cover lemma, and Noetherianness from a finite affine cover. Step 6 gets affine W_i around each generic point inside the complement of the other components, so R_i is a domain. Step 7 is the denominator argument, written out: s = product of generator denominators gives (C_i)_s = (R_i)_s. Step 8 glues the isomorphisms, and U is dense. Edge cases checked: empty X, a field, a normal domain, k[x,y]/(xy) and k[t²,t³]. New node lem-per-componentwise-normalization-affine-charts: it is 035P(1),(3),(4) plus 0CDV, and it is true. Neither assumption gives this fact, so it is genuinely outside the assumed statements and the citation is accepted. No SGA source is cited. No fixes.
